questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Asymptote of a Rational Function
questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{9{x}^{5}+3{x}^{2}+11}{12{x}^{5}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{9{x}^{5}+3{x}^{2}+11}{12{x}^{5}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{9{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{11}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{12{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(9+\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{11}{{x}^{5}})}{(12)} \\  & =\frac{9+0+0}{12} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=\frac{3}{4}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{4{x}^{2}-9x+1}{x+4}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{4{x}^{2}-9x+1}{x+4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4{x}^{2}}{x}-\frac{9x}{x}+\frac{1}{x})}{(\frac{x}{x}+\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x-9+\frac{1}{x})}{(1+\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x-9+0)}{(1+0)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(4x)-9 \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity: Infinite Solutions
questions.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{4{x}^{5}-9}{{x}^{3}+8x} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{4{x}^{5}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{8x}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(4{x}^{2}-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})}{(1+\frac{8}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{4{x}^{2}-0}{1+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }4{x}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{5+7{x}^{3}}{12x}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5+7{x}^{3}}{12x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{5}{x}+\frac{7{x}^{3}}{x})}{(\frac{12x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{5}{x}+7{x}^{2})}{12} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(0+7{x}^{2})}{12} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity: Infinite Solutions
questions.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{{x}^{7}-3{x}^{2}+4x}{{x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+5} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{{x}^{7}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{4x}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{3{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{({x}^{3}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{4}{{x}^{3}})}{(1-\frac{3}{x}+\frac{5}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{({x}^{3}-0+0)}{(1-0+0)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,{x}^{3} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity: Infinite Solutions
